extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, communicators, and media/press-release writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating contemporary, multimedia-forward press releases that attract journalists and generate earned media by combining strong fundamentals (clear headlines, credibility, formatting) with visual and distribution strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise headline with action words and who/what/why
rubrics_metrics.description: Has a concise headline that includes action words (e.g. “reveals,” “shows,” “announces,” etc.) and clearly articulates the who, what and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use active verbs and make the headline communicate the core news immediately so a journalist can tell the story at a glance. Avoid vague or clickbait headlines; prioritize clarity about who is involved, what happened/launched, and why it matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include compelling, high-quality visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes compelling, high-quality visuals: photos, videos, infographics or data visualizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visuals improve reach and engagement; research cited shows higher engagement for releases with images. Prefer high-resolution, professionally produced assets. Where possible include more than one image and tailor formats (photos, infographics, short video) to potential outlet needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature content that adds credibility and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Features content that adds credibility and validation: unique data or research, testimonials or quotes from experts or executives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide original data, research findings, expert commentary or executive quotes to validate claims and give journalists credible sourcing and story hooks. Avoid unsupported claims and promotional fluff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format strategically for readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Is formatted strategically (e.g. employs bullets, subheads, bolded text and short paragraphs) to break up the text and make the information easy to consume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure releases so busy journalists can scan quickly. Use bullets, subheads and short paragraphs; bold key facts. Break up dense blocks of copy to increase the chance of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid jargon, clichés and marketing speak
rubrics_metrics.description: Does not have any jargon, clichés or 'marketing speak'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write plainly and objectively. Use clear news language rather than promotional or buzzword-heavy phrasing so journalists perceive the release as usable reporting material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point to a clear call to action with links
rubrics_metrics.description: Points to a clear call to action, with links back to the brand’s website, press room or social media accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit CTAs and working links so journalists and readers can find more information, assets, or contact points. Link to press kits, landing pages, or social channels as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include brand logo and make it easy to include
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes a brand logo to reinforce brand awareness — and makes it easy for the media outlet to include in their coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide logo files (proper formats/sizes) and clear permission so outlets can reuse them. This reinforces brand recognition and simplifies editors' workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure relevance to the journalist’s audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Your press release must be relevant to the audience of the journalist who sees it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor content and targeting so the story aligns with the beat and readership of each journalist or outlet. Relevance is emphasized as a requirement — irrelevant releases are unlikely to get coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make multimedia elements repurposable and eye-catching
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-crafted press release includes pithy, eye-catching elements such as quotes, short videos or infographics that can easily be repurposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create assets (sound bites, short clips, graphics) that can be reused across channels (web, social, earned coverage). Consider producing short-form social videos for owned/paid/earned distribution to extend reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider multichannel news releases (MNR) and visual-forward web pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multichannel news release (MNR): visual-forward content with multimedia components, such as videos, interactive charts and infographics published as web pages and syndicated to targeted media outlets and journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MNRs act like a wire service for multimedia storytelling—publish as rich web pages that can be syndicated. Use interactive/visual formats when the story benefits from data visualization or video to make coverage easier and more engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in long-term relationships and journalist research
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing credibility and trust are paramount — do your homework to understand the journalist’s audience and what they find relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and use a media management database, review past contact lists, and research who has covered relevant topics and outlets. Personalized, relevant outreach increases likelihood of engagement and coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner with distribution platforms offering monitoring and consulting
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnering with a distribution platform that offers sophisticated media monitoring technologies and expert strategic consulting can help PR practitioners target and cultivate relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use platform tools to identify likely journalists, monitor coverage, and free up time for relationship-building and content creation. Platforms can improve targeting efficiency and strategic distribution.
